binary_version: minotari 0.2.0 (cargo build --release from tari-project/minotari-cli current main)
summary: Mode 2 has no documented path to perform a genesis rescan on an existing wallet. The minotari-cli `re-scan --rescan-from-height 0` rolls back DB state (BlockRolledBack events, soft-deleted outputs/inputs, scanned tip blocks deleted to height 0) but does NOT reset the wallet's last_scanned_height value. When the daemon is next started, it reads the stale last_scanned_height and resumes from there - in this run, observed last_scanned_height after re-scan and daemon restart = 670400 (the tip-adjacent value from before the re-scan).
wallet_seed_words: doctor exist smoke swing sibling okay endless unusual tent soda wire badge happy vague monster maximum cherry quiz crash friend crunch lumber unique vintage

re_scan_subprocess.stdout_summary: Many BlockRolledBack events, Soft deleting inputs/outputs, Deleting scanned tip blocks, then Re-scan complete event_count=0

implication_for_other_scenarios: S2 (genesis rescan after S1) - same blocker
S3 (birthday rescan) - measurable: blocks_scanned = tip - birthday_at_create
S7 (birthday rescan, checkpoint 2) - measurable: same path as S3
intended_path_per_spec_author: SWvheerden 2026-05-29 wallet-benchmarks#1: 'change the seed words so that the encoded birthday reflects 0'. No CLI flag or API endpoint on minotari-cli current main implements this.
recommended_minotari_change: Add --birthday flag to `minotari create` subcommand, or expose a daemon endpoint POST /accounts/{name}/set_birthday that updates the DB row and triggers a full re-scan from the new birthday.
